correctness.rationale: For each \(m\ge1\), the polynomial \(h_m\) has exactly the prescribed \(m+1\) simple zeros on the slit. The piecewise function \(f_m\) is continuous and semialgebraic on the slit disk because the slit removes the sign discontinuity and \(h_m(0)=0\). The displayed homotopy fixes the negative first coordinate while collapsing the second coordinate and radially collapses the nonnegative half-disk; it therefore preserves the graph closure and fixes \(A_m\) pointwise. The retract graph has \(m+1\) vertices and \(2m\) edges, so its cycle rank is exactly \(m\). Michel's section-transfer proposition then gives a bounded CAD cell in \(\mathbf R^4\) with the same closure topology.

value.rationale: The result turns a qualitative failure of contractibility into an unbounded-complexity theorem in fixed ambient dimension. First Betti number and free fundamental-group rank are natural topological invariants for cell-closure behavior, directly relevant to the regularity assumptions used in CAD topology and algorithms. The family is structural rather than an arbitrary parameter slice: each added zero of \(h_m\) creates one new independent boundary cycle, giving an exact and transparent complexity mechanism.
